```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

artifact_dir <- params$artifact_dir
audit <- fread(file.path(artifact_dir, "data_audit.csv"))
daily <- fread(file.path(artifact_dir, "daily_summary.csv"))
priority <- fread(file.path(artifact_dir, "priority_dates.csv"))
sensitivity <- fread(file.path(artifact_dir, "score_sensitivity.csv"))

n_records <- audit[check == "Source records", value]
n_fields <- audit[check == "Usable source fields", value]
missing_arrivals <- audit[check == "Missing arrival delay", value]
top_day <- as.Date(priority$FL_DATE[[1]])
top_late <- priority$late15_rate[[1]]
top_mean <- priority$mean_arrival_delay[[1]]
top_p95 <- priority$p95_arrival_delay[[1]]
```

# Purpose

This report is a portfolio reanalysis of a January 2019 U.S. flight extract.
It asks two deliberately limited questions:

1. Is the supplied file internally consistent enough for delay analysis?
2. Which dates deserve further operational review based on several transparent
   delay-severity measures?

The analysis produces an investigation queue, not a causal claim about an
airline, airport, weather event, or operational failure.

# Data audit

The supplied extract contains `r format(n_records, big.mark = ",")` records and
`r n_fields` usable fields. It does not include carrier, flight number,
cancellation/diversion, scheduled time, weather, or delay-cause fields. Missing
arrival outcomes are retained and reported rather than silently treated as
on-time flights.

```{r audit-table}
kable(audit, caption = "Internal data-quality checks", align = c("l", "r"))
```

```{r missingness-figure, out.width='78%', fig.align='center'}
include_graphics(file.path(artifact_dir, "missingness.png"))
```

The `r format(missing_arrivals, big.mark = ",")` records without an arrival-delay
outcome may include materially disrupted flights. Consequently, all severity
rates are conditional on known arrival outcomes and may understate disruption.

# Daily disruption profile

For each date, the review calculates flight volume, missing-outcome rate, mean
and median arrival delay, the 95th percentile, the share at least 15 minutes
late, the share at least 60 minutes late, and the share that worsened by at
least 60 minutes after departure.

```{r late-rate-figure, out.width='96%', fig.align='center'}
include_graphics(file.path(artifact_dir, "daily_late15_rate.png"))
```

```{r severity-figure, out.width='96%', fig.align='center'}
include_graphics(file.path(artifact_dir, "daily_delay_severity.png"))
```

# Priority dates

The priority score is the average percentile rank across five measures: mean
delay, 95th-percentile delay, late-15 rate, severe-60 rate, and post-departure
worsening rate. It is a relative review score within January 2019, not a
probability or calibrated anomaly confidence.

The highest-scoring date is **`r format(top_day, '%B %d, %Y')`**. Among flights
with known arrival outcomes, `r percent(top_late, accuracy = 0.1)` arrived at
least 15 minutes late; mean arrival delay was `r number(top_mean, accuracy=0.1)`
minutes and the 95th percentile was `r number(top_p95, accuracy=1)` minutes.

```{r priority-table}
display_priority <- priority[1:10, .(
  Date = as.Date(FL_DATE),
  Flights = flights,
  `Known arrivals` = known_arrivals,
  `Missing arrival outcome` = percent(arrival_missing_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
  `Mean delay (min)` = round(mean_arrival_delay, 1),
  `P95 delay (min)` = round(p95_arrival_delay, 1),
  `Late 15+` = percent(late15_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
  `Priority score` = round(priority_score, 1)
)]
kable(display_priority, caption = "Highest-priority dates for follow-up review")
```

# Sensitivity check

To check whether one measure alone drives the ranking, the score is recalculated
five times, each time leaving out one component. The table reports how many of
the original top five dates remain.

```{r sensitivity-table}
kable(sensitivity, caption = "Leave-one-metric-out priority-score sensitivity")
```

# Limitations

- Known-arrival statistics can be biased if missing outcomes represent the most
  disrupted flights.
- The file lacks carrier, schedule, cancellation/diversion, weather, and causal
  delay fields.
- Daily observations are not independent flight-level experiments.
- The composite score is a triage device and should be paired with source-record
  review and external operational context.
- A later month or external event labels would be required for genuine
  out-of-sample validation.
